about.title: About Apsis
about.intro: Apsis is a tool for the design of trajectories in the solar system. The Explorer mode shows a flight in a 3D view. The Expert mode shows the plan, the maneuvers and all numbers. The two modes use one engine and the same data.

manual.note: The user manual opens in a new tab of the browser.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.local: This browser does all calculations. No server does calculations for the application, and the application has no user accounts.
privacy.network: The application gets only its files from the web server. It sends no data, and it gets no data from other computers.
privacy.tracking: The application does not record your operations. It uses no cookies.
privacy.storage: The storage of this browser keeps your settings, your saved missions and the bodies that you added.
privacy.links: A link on this page opens a web page of a different owner. That owner can record that you opened the page.
privacy.clearQuestion: Remove your settings, your saved missions and your bodies from this browser? The application then starts again and the open mission closes.

view.title: The 3D view
view.engine: The engine calculates each flight path on the screen. The 3D view and the tables show the same results. The application has no stored flight paths.
view.aids: Names, orbit lines and symbols help you to find objects. They are not physical objects.
view.notes: In the 3D view, the button with the letter i shows how the application made the picture of the body in view.

data.title: Data of the engine
data.intro: The application contains all the data that it uses. The data come from the sources below.
data.planets: Positions of the Sun, the planets, the Moon and the Pluto system
data.centers: Center of a planet that has moons
data.small: Positions of the asteroids, the comets and the dwarf planets
data.accuracy: The Accuracy screen shows the measured differences from JPL Horizons and from published values. It also gives the limits of the models and the items that have no check.

maps.title: Maps of the bodies
maps.intro: Each map comes from the data of a space mission, of a telescope or of star catalogs. The list gives the credit, the license and the source of each file, and the changes that the project made.
maps.noMap: A body that is not in this list has no map. The application calculates its picture.
maps.failed: The application cannot read the list of the maps.

models.title: Spacecraft models
models.original: The project made the spacecraft models for this application. The code makes each model and each of its surfaces. The models use no file from other software.
models.look: Each model shows approximately the shape of one type of spacecraft. It is not an accurate copy of an actual spacecraft. The surfaces show materials only: no symbols and no text.
models.apsis: The spacecraft of your missions is a design of the project. It is not an actual spacecraft.
models.attitude: The 3D view shows an example attitude. The trajectory calculation does not use the attitude or the shape of the spacecraft.

software.title: Software
software.intro: The files of the application contain these libraries.
software.fonts: The application uses the fonts of your computer. It contains no font files. The project made the logo and the icons for this application.
software.music: Music: the application makes the music while it operates, with the Web Audio interface of the browser. It uses no recorded music.

names.title: Names
names.text: Apsis is an independent project. It has no relation with a space agency or with the owner of a different product. The names of missions, of spacecraft and of products only tell you which item the text is about.
